items.title: Why Cybersecurity Basics Will Always Matter — Even With AI
items.summary: AI is reshaping how we work and learn at UBC. It can streamline tasks, support research, and spark innovation. But as AI tools advance, so do the techniques used by cybercriminals. items.title: Predictability: The Enemy of Online Safety
items.summary: Cybercriminals are not searching for chaos—they’re searching for patterns . In a large, complex environment like UBC, where faculty and staff rely on well-established routines to keep work moving, those habits can unintentionally create a roadmap for attackers. items.title: Reputation Security: Understanding Your Digital Legacy
items.summary: At UBC, we work with sensitive information every day—from research data to financial details to personal records. items.title: Why No One Is “Too Small” to Be a Victim of Cybercrime
items.summary: Many people believe cybercriminals only go after big companies, high-profile individuals, or people with large financial resources. items.title: Fake Order Confirmation Emails Are Leading to Phone Scams
items.summary: UBC has received multiple reports of emails claiming a printer order was just placed using the recipient's account, sent under the names of real companies like Staples and Dell.
